what: KT Corporation is South Korea's largest fixed-line and broadband operator and its second-largest mobile carrier, and it runs a growing cloud, data centre and media business.
customers: South Korean households and businesses on phone, broadband and television subscriptions.
money: enterprise IT, media, finance and property
moat: The national fixed-line network, built when KT was the state monopoly, which no competitor could replicate and which underpins broadband and enterprise services.
risks: Korean telecom is saturated and tariffs are under political pressure
Revenue has been roughly flat for five years
Only four analysts cover the American listing
opportunities: 9.2 times earnings and 4.6 times EBITDA with $817M of free cash flow
Its data centre and cloud business serves a country short of capacity and growing fast
watch: Enterprise and cloud revenue growth against flat telecom revenue.
